name: Relay.app
tagline: AI agent workflow automation platform pitched as the new Zapier
description: Relay.app, a human-in-the-loop AI workflow automation tool founded by former Google product director Jacob Bank, raised $8.1M before shutting down in 2026. Bank and some staff joined Google's Chrome team, but Google did not acquire the company, its product or its IP.
story:
Relay was founded in July 2021 by Jacob Bank, who had joined Google in 2015 when it acquired his scheduling startup Timeful and went on to work on Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Chat. He built Relay's early team largely from former Gmail and Calendar colleagues. The company emerged in October 2022 with a $5M seed round led by Khosla Ventures, pitching a modern alternative to Zapier for teams of 30 to 500 people. Its distinguishing feature was human-in-the-loop automation: workflows could pause for a person to review, approve or supply data before continuing. A further $3.1M round led by Andreessen Horowitz in 2023 brought total funding to about $8.1M. As large language models matured, Relay repositioned around AI steps and agents, adding MCP servers, sequences and tables.

In July 2026 Relay told customers it was shutting down. Free accounts lost access on August 15, 2026, and paid accounts were given until September 14. Users could export workflows, run history and tables to rebuild elsewhere. The notice gave no reason. On August 17, TechCrunch reported that Bank was rejoining Google as VP of Product for Chrome, with some Relay staff following him. Coverage described the move as a hire rather than an acquisition: Google did not buy the company, its product or its IP, and no deal terms or investor returns were reported.

Relay never publicly explained the decision. Commentators pointed to the pressure on standalone automation tools as Google Workspace, Microsoft Copilot and OpenAI build agentic features into products customers already pay for. Its end follows a now familiar pattern: the team found a new home inside a platform company, and the product was switched off.
